• Scientific name: Trichomycterus mirissumba Costa, 1992
  • Type locality: Rio Preto, near junction with the Santa Clara Creek, Rio Paraiba basin, Visconde de Mauá, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
  • IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated
South America: Preto River, Paraíba do Sul River basin in Brazil. Rio de Janeiro State Rivers, Paraíba do Sul, Preto (Minas Gerais).

South America: Preto River, Paraíba do Sul River basin (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil). Type locality: Visconde de Mauá, 1 km east of the village of Maromba, Preto River, near the confluence with the Santa Clara stream, Paraíba River basin, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

Trichomycterus mirissumba is endemic to the middle portion of the Paraíba do Sul River basin, in the states of Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro. The species is not very abundant and infrequent, found within the limits of the Serra da Mantiqueira APA.
This genus takes live or frozen food, and commercial dry prepared foods are also well accepted. Be careful not to overfeed. In nature, they feed on small invertebrates living at the bottom.
Unreported in the aquarium. There is no breeding report.

Etymology: the specific name mirissumba is the local name for this catfish in the village of Maromba (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil), probably derived from Tupí-Guaraní, its meaning unknown (tadpoles).

IUCN Red List: the species is scarce and infrequent, found within the boundaries of the Serra da Mantiqueira Environmental Protection Area. No significant threats have been identified; therefore, the taxon has been categorised as Least Concern (LC) (IUCN 2022).
